doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Coltrane as Ali's guru
summary: Ali credits Coltrane with giving him the chance to develop, as Miles had for Coltrane.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Of all the guys that you’ve worked with, this could be for both of you, is there someone who was the best at giving you suggestions or directions, that helped you? Is there a person that comes to mind?

He was my guru man. He was my everything. He did, as far as I’m concerned, he did it all. And I was very fortunate that he took a liking to me and brought me in and sort of directed — well not directed — but sort of gave me the privilege to explore my playing. He helped me to develop what I was trying to do. Because he saw what I was trying to do. And he just put me in a position to develop it. And he told me that, because Miles Davis did the same thing for him. He saw the potential in Coltrane and he put him in a position where he can develop that stuff that he was doing. And the same thing happened for me. John brought me in there knowing that I had something, and just gave me a chance to do it. And he would always say, “All you need to do,” and I always tell young musicians, ones that I like a lot, “all you need to do is to keep playing. Just get with somebody that you can play and it will come to you.” And I don’t care what it is that your playing, as long as you’re playing and searching and trying to do this it will happen for you. So I think he made it happen for me. He gave me a chance to make it happen.
